Native Village of Chitina

This guide introduces the Native Village of Chitina through a state historical study and Chitina Native Corporation’s public history. The sources connect Chitina with lower Ahtna communities and the Copper River, while helping distinguish the Tribe from the separately incorporated business organization and the wider settlement.

01

Ahtna connections and a changing settlement

Fall and Simeone’s historical background places the Chitina area within a network of lower Ahtna communities whose salmon use long preceded the railway town. The authors explain Chitina’s name through Tsedi Na’, the Ahtna name for the Chitina River. They describe a settlement that grew during railway construction in 1909–1911 and drew people from surrounding villages. Their account also emphasizes continued connections after later out-migration: a reduced resident population did not mean the place ceased to be home. This is a historical synthesis with an expressly limited reviewed passage, rather than a claim to represent every family’s experience.

Read the sources [1] Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Subsistence

02

Keeping the Village and corporation distinct

Chitina Native Corporation’s history identifies the Native Village of Chitina as the local Tribe and describes the corporation as a separate organization incorporated in 1973, with shareholders primarily residents or descendants of the Village. Its sketches of historical leaders credit Chief Nicolai with assisting early exploration parties and identify Chief Hanagita as a later lower Ahtna leader. Read these as attributed corporate historical accounts. The page’s old settlement figures do not establish current tribal membership, and its business history does not explain the Tribe’s full governmental history.

Read the sources [2] Chitina Native Corporation

Customary and Traditional Use Worksheet: Salmon, Chitina Subdistrict, Prince William Sound Management Area (Special Publication SP2002-001) ↗

Publication: 2002 (prepared for December 2002 meeting)

Selected historical background explains Chitina’s relationship to older Ahtna communities and later railway settlement.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Title/citation pages (PDF pp.1, 3–5); contents; complete printed p.13 (PDF p.22), especially Historical Background. Local text and complete rendered p.13 read. Other pages were machine-extracted for finding the passage but were not substantively reviewed.

Native corporation historyChitina Native CorporationSource 2

History — Chitina Native Corporation ↗

Corporate account distinguishes its 1973 incorporation from the Native Village and provides short profiles of historical Ahtna leaders.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Read the entire page: corporate history, relationship to Native Village of Chitina and six named historical biographies. Distinguishes shareholders from the separate local tribe. Leadership, family and place-name accounts are attributed corporate public history; approximate dates retain their uncertainty. The 2004 population estimate is historical, not current, and no ceremonial explanation is reproduced.

Review recorded: October 20, 2026

Access note: Public main body was read through the web reader; navigation and unrelated content were excluded. Original 2026-10-20 review dates and full original annotation scope are retained from the existing Ahtna collection. The 2026-11-02 selected verification is recorded separately; this work is not globally new.
